claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a significant caloric response.
The as-cast alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
Surface mechanical attrition treatment followed by light annealing will produce an ultrafine-grained surface layer.
Surface mechanical attrition treatment followed by light annealing will leave compressive residual stresses in the surface layer.
The treated surface layer will be harder and tougher than the untreated surface.
Annealing at approximately 600 °C for 1 hour will relax excessive surface stresses.
Annealing at approximately 600 °C for 1 hour will not promote bulk phase changes.
The compressive residual stress will counteract tensile stresses during mechanical loading.
Counteracting tensile stresses at the surface will reduce surface crack initiation.
Counteracting tensile stresses at the surface will reduce crack propagation.
The proposed treatment will leave the bulk microstructure chemically and structurally unaltered.
The bulk matrix governs the alloy's magnetocaloric and barocaloric transitions.
Preserving the bulk matrix will preserve the caloric response under applied magnetic fields and pressures.
The treatment will significantly improve resistance to surface-initiated cracking.
The treatment will enhance overall load-bearing integrity.
The treated alloy will retain caloric performance equivalent to that of the untreated alloy under similar magnetic and pressure fields.
The untreated alloy's poor integrity arises from brittle behavior, surface-initiated cracking, and casting defects.
The treatment will remain effective only while mechanical loading stays below levels that cause failure within the thin treated layer.
